The pruning criterion controls whether reinforcement learning succeeds or fails during recovery of a compressed reasoning model. Yet this dramatic difference in training dynamics leaves downstream accuracy unchanged: under fine-grained structured pruning at moderate sparsity, RL and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) recover the pruned model to the same accuracy regardless of criterion. \section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

Structured pruning compresses reasoning Large Language Models (LLMs) by removing entire groups of feed-forward channels, but the pruned model must recover its reasoning capabilities through fine-tuning.
A natural question is which recovery paradigm to use.
Recent work gives a clear answer: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) substantially outperforms supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and restores pruned reasoning models to near-original accuracy~\citep{selfhealing2025}.
This hierarchy creates a testable prediction: a pruning criterion that better preserves the model's ability to benefit from RL should yield higher accuracy after recovery.

Our experiments challenge this prediction.
On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B~\citep{deepseek2025r1} pruned to 20\% MLP channel sparsity, one criterion achieves 4.4 times the peak RL reward of another under GRPO~\citep{shao2024grpo}, yet for each criterion individually, SFT and GRPO recover the model to within 1 percentage point of each other.
The pruning criterion determines whether RL training succeeds or fails, but has minimal effect on final accuracy.
We term this pattern \emph{reward-accuracy decoupling}: RL reward, ostensibly a proxy for task performance, diverges from accuracy under structured pruning.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/paper/fig1_dose_response.pdf}
\caption{Dose-response curve for the CKA diversity coefficient $\alpha$ at 20\% MLP channel sparsity on GSM8K ($N{=}1{,}319$). Recovery accuracy follows an inverted-U, peaking at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\%). SFT and GRPO curves nearly overlap ($|\Delta| \leq 1.14$\,pp at every point), illustrating reward-accuracy decoupling.}
\label{fig:dose_response}
\end{figure}

This disconnect is surprising in light of recent mechanistic work.
RL compresses incorrect reasoning paths while SFT expands correct ones~\citep{rlsqueezes2026}.
These asymmetric pressures predict that the two paradigms should complement each other, not converge to the same outcome.
Yet existing structured pruning methods for reasoning LLMs~\citep{graspprune2026,resp2025,llmpruner2023,bonsai2025} optimize for immediate post-pruning quality without examining how the criterion shapes RL recovery.
No prior work has compared multiple criteria under RL or tested whether the ``RLVR $>$ SFT'' advantage persists across pruning strategies.
\citet{selfhealing2025} evaluate unstructured magnitude pruning at 96.5\% parameter retention; our structural removal of entire channel groups may impose different demands on recovery.

We investigate through Recovery-Aware Structured Pruning (\rasp{}), a scoring function that combines gradient importance with CKA-based representational diversity~\citep{kornblith2019cka}.
A single coefficient $\alpha$ controls the balance (Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}): the dose-response curve reveals an inverted-U in recovery accuracy, peaking at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\% on GSM8K;~\citealp{cobbe2021gsm8k}).
Under GRPO, the four criteria span a \textbf{recovery capacity spectrum} that tracks preserved diversity rather than importance: criteria that maximize diversity sustain RL training, while importance-dominated criteria fail to learn.
The SFT and GRPO curves in Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response} nearly overlap at every $\alpha$, confirming decoupling across the full spectrum.
A depth pruning baseline (ShortGPT;~\citealp{shortgpt2024}) is the sole exception ($-$1.36\,pp on GSM8K), which suggests that pruning granularity interacts with RL trainability.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Reward-accuracy decoupling.} At 20--25\% fine-grained MLP sparsity, SFT and GRPO yield equivalent accuracy regardless of pruning criterion, confirmed by TOST equivalence testing for CKA-only and Standard, with all criteria showing comparable deltas. At 15\%, GRPO amplifies the CKA-guided advantage, which delineates the boundary of this phenomenon (\S\ref{sec:decoupling}).
    \item \textbf{Recovery capacity spectrum.} \rasp{} reveals that four pruning criteria produce qualitatively distinct RL dynamics. Dose-response analysis traces an inverted-U in recovery, with preliminary evidence across scales and models within the Qwen2.5 family (\S\ref{sec:scoring}, \S\ref{sec:recovery_gradient}, \S\ref{sec:extended_analysis}).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/paper/fig1_method_framework.pdf}
\caption{Overview of our pruning comparison framework. \textbf{Left}: structural analysis computes importance $I(h)$ and CKA-based overlap $F(h)$ scores, which four scoring criteria combine differently (Eqs.~\ref{eq:standard}--\ref{eq:cka_only}). \textbf{Center}: ranked structures are removed up to the target sparsity, subject to per-layer capacity floors. \textbf{Right}: all pruned models undergo identical two-stage recovery (SFT warmup $\to$ GRPO). \textbf{Bottom}: the resulting recovery capacity spectrum, from active learning (CKA-only) to training failure (\rasp{} at $\alpha{=}1.0$), tracks preserved representational diversity rather than gradient importance.}
\label{fig:method_framework}
\end{figure*}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

Structured pruning compresses reasoning Large Language Models (LLMs) by removing entire channel groups, but the pruned model must recover through fine-tuning.
\citet{selfhealing2025} show that reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) substantially outperforms supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for this recovery.
This positions RLVR as the dominant paradigm and creates a testable prediction: a pruning criterion that preserves the model's capacity for RL exploration should yield higher final accuracy.
The evidence, however, comes from unstructured magnitude pruning at 96.5\% parameter retention; whether the RLVR advantage holds under structural compression, which removes entire computational units and alters the architecture, remains untested.

Our experiments reveal that it does not.
On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B~\citep{deepseek2025r1} pruned to 20\% MLP channel sparsity, one criterion achieves 4.4 times the peak RL reward of another (CKA-only vs.\ Standard) under GRPO~\citep{shao2024grpo}, yet for each criterion individually, SFT and GRPO recover the model to within 1 percentage point of each other.
The pruning criterion determines whether RL training succeeds or collapses, but this stark difference leaves almost no trace in final accuracy.
We term this pattern \emph{reward-accuracy decoupling}.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/paper/fig1_dose_response.pdf}
\caption{Dose-response curve for the CKA diversity coefficient $\alpha$ at 20\% MLP channel sparsity on GSM8K ($N{=}1{,}319$). Recovery accuracy follows an inverted-U, peaking at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\%). SFT and GRPO curves nearly overlap ($|\Delta| \leq 1.14$\,pp at every point), illustrating reward-accuracy decoupling.}
\label{fig:dose_response}
\end{figure}

This disconnect is surprising in light of recent mechanistic work.
RL compresses incorrect reasoning paths while SFT expands correct ones~\citep{rlsqueezes2026}.
These asymmetric pressures predict that the two paradigms should complement each other, not converge to the same outcome.
Yet existing structured pruning methods for reasoning LLMs~\citep{graspprune2026,resp2025,llmpruner2023,bonsai2025} optimize for immediate post-pruning quality without examining how the criterion shapes RL recovery.
No prior work has compared multiple criteria under RL or tested whether the ``RLVR $>$ SFT'' advantage persists across pruning strategies.

To investigate systematically, we introduce Recovery-Aware Structured Pruning (\rasp{}), a scoring function that combines gradient importance with CKA-based representational diversity~\citep{kornblith2019cka}.
A single coefficient $\alpha$ controls the balance (Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}): the dose-response curve reveals an inverted-U in recovery accuracy, peaking at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\% on GSM8K;~\citealp{cobbe2021gsm8k}).
Under GRPO, the four criteria span a \textbf{recovery capacity spectrum} that tracks preserved diversity rather than importance: criteria that maximize diversity sustain RL training, while importance-dominated criteria fail to learn.
The SFT and GRPO curves in Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response} nearly overlap at every $\alpha$, which confirms decoupling across the full spectrum.
A depth pruning baseline (ShortGPT;~\citealp{shortgpt2024}) is the sole exception ($-$1.36\,pp on GSM8K), which suggests that pruning granularity interacts with RL trainability.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Reward-accuracy decoupling.} At 20--25\% fine-grained MLP sparsity, SFT and GRPO yield equivalent accuracy regardless of pruning criterion, confirmed by TOST equivalence testing for CKA-only and Standard, with all criteria within comparable margins. At 15\%, GRPO amplifies the CKA-guided advantage, delineating the boundary (\S\ref{sec:decoupling}).
    \item \textbf{Recovery capacity spectrum.} \rasp{} reveals that four pruning criteria produce qualitatively distinct RL dynamics. Dose-response analysis traces an inverted-U in recovery, with preliminary evidence across scales and models within the Qwen2.5 family (\S\ref{sec:scoring}, \S\ref{sec:recovery_gradient}, \S\ref{sec:extended_analysis}).
    \item \textbf{SFT warmup as the dominant recovery mechanism.} Across all criteria and sparsity levels, SFT warmup recovers from near-zero post-prune accuracy to 51--64\%, while subsequent GRPO adds less than 1\,pp. This dominance persists at 300 training steps. RL reward trajectories instead serve as structural diagnostics that reveal pruning deficiencies invisible to accuracy (\S\ref{sec:decoupling}, \S\ref{sec:extended_analysis}).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/paper/fig1_method_framework.pdf}
\caption{Overview of our pruning comparison framework. \textbf{Left}: structural analysis computes importance $I(h)$ and CKA-based overlap $F(h)$ scores, which four scoring criteria combine differently (Eqs.~\ref{eq:standard}--\ref{eq:cka_only}). \textbf{Center}: ranked structures are removed up to the target sparsity, subject to per-layer capacity floors. \textbf{Right}: all pruned models undergo identical two-stage recovery (SFT warmup $\to$ GRPO). \textbf{Bottom}: the resulting recovery capacity spectrum, from active learning (CKA-only) to training failure (\rasp{} at $\alpha{=}1.0$), tracks preserved representational diversity rather than gradient importance.}
\label{fig:method_framework}
\end{figure*}

108	\subsection{Two-Stage Recovery}
109	\label{sec:recovery}
110	
111	After pruning, all four models undergo identical two-stage recovery: (1)~a brief SFT warmup on chain-of-thought demonstrations restores end-of-sequence generation and format compliance (pruning disrupts termination behavior, making direct GRPO infeasible); (2)~GRPO with binary reward enables RL-based exploration, redistributing functionality across remaining structures~\citep{rlsqueezes2026}, in contrast to SFT which imitates fixed trajectories.
112	Details in Section~\ref{sec:exp_setup} and Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_training}.

114	\subsection{Recovery Capacity Diagnostics}
115	\label{sec:diagnostics}
116	
117	We define \textbf{recovery capacity} as the model's ability to benefit from post-pruning recovery training, operationalized as peak mean reward over the GRPO training horizon.
118	Four diagnostics (mean reward, zero-variance batch fraction ($f_0$), gradient norm, and Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence) distinguish three regimes: \emph{active learning} (rising reward, low $f_0$), \emph{stagnation} (flat reward), and \emph{collapse} (declining reward, high $f_0$, vanishing gradients).
119

1	Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is widely regarded as essential for recovering pruned reasoning models, substantially outperforming supervised fine-tuning (SFT). We find that this advantage vanishes under fine-grained structured pruning: across four criteria applied to a 7B reasoning model at moderate sparsity, SFT and RL recover to the same accuracy regardless of criterion. We term this \emph{reward-accuracy decoupling}.
2	What the pruning criterion does control is RL training dynamics. To study this, we introduce Recovery-Aware Structured Pruning (\rasp{}), a scoring function that balances gradient importance with representational diversity via Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA). The resulting \emph{recovery capacity spectrum} shows that diversity-preserving criteria sustain RL optimization while importance-dominated criteria fail entirely, yet none of these differences translate into accuracy gains over SFT.
3	These findings reframe the role of RL in pruning recovery: SFT warmup captures most recoverable reasoning capacity, while RL serves as a diagnostic that reveals structural deficiencies invisible to accuracy. Directional trends hold across three benchmarks, with preliminary cross-scale and cross-model evidence\footnote{Code and data are available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/recovery_aware_struct_prune-5FA5/}.}.
